newsitem.title: INDIA: Indian metals steady in dull trade.
newsitem.headline: Indian metals steady in dull trade.

text.p: Indian base metals were steady at lower levels on Friday, dealers said.
"Fresh demand from industrial consumers was sluggish but reports of a rally in world markets checked the fall in domestic prices, one dealer said.
Copper was steady at 13,450 rupees per quintal after dropping 50 rupees on Wednesday.
The metal market was closed on Thursday for a local holiday.
Zinc was unchanged at 7,750 rupees and lead steady at 4,200 rupees per quintal. Both were down 50 rupees per quintal on Wednesday.
Other metals which were unchanged were aluminium at 7,450 rupees, tin at 31,200 rupees and nickel at 36,100 rupees per quintal but dealers said trade was light.

"Overall supplies remained low in the local market at the lower levels," said Sharad Parikh, president of Bombay Metal Exchange. "Looking at the rising global prices, local prices may also rise if there is some fresh buying support."
